# 0021. Student PIN login, auto-generated student_number, and profile pictures

## Status
Accepted

## Context
Raised by the user after a separate frontend session (a companion project, not part of this repo) started integrating against this backend and surfaced two real gaps: `student_number` was caller-supplied only with no server-side generation, and there was no student-facing login simpler than email+password. The frontend also needed profile pictures for both students and staff. This is the first stage to add a second authentication path or any file-upload capability to this backend.

Three genuine design forks were raised as explicit questions and confirmed before finalizing the plan, not decided silently: PIN-generation RBAC tier (ADMIN-only, matching the precedent already set for Users — credential issuance is a different trust level than academic-record editing), PIN-login rate-limit strictness (kept at the existing 5/minute-per-IP floor), and who can upload profile pictures (admin-tier only, matching each domain's existing mutation gate — no self-upload `/me` routes for now).

## Decision

### Auto-generated `student_number`
A Postgres sequence (`student_number_seq`, created via `op.execute("CREATE SEQUENCE ...")` in the migration, not a SQLAlchemy-modeled column) backs generation, not a retry-on-conflict loop — `nextval()` is atomically race-safe by construction, consistent with this codebase's existing preference for DB-native mechanisms over reinvented ones (e.g. `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` in `UserRepository.count_active_super_admins`). `StudentCreate.student_number` became `str | None = None`; `StudentService.create()` generates and formats (`STU-0001`) only when omitted, and manual override still works with no format validation imposed. The existing uniqueness pre-check + `IntegrityError`-catch pattern (ADR 0004) runs against the final value regardless of source, since the sequence only prevents collisions among generated values, not against a manually-supplied one.

### Student PIN login
`Student.pin_hash: str | None` lives on `Student`, not `User` — keeps `User` role-agnostic (every existing `User` column applies to every role; `pin_hash` would be the first one-role-only column there) and keeps the lookup-then-verify pair (`student_number` + `pin_hash`) on the same row, the same cohesion reasoning `hashed_password` on `User` already follows.

**The `DUMMY_PASSWORD_HASH` trap.** `src/sms/core/security.py`'s `DUMMY_PASSWORD_HASH` is a fixed, source-controlled Argon2 hash used only to keep hashing cost constant on the failure path of the oracle defense (`login()`, and now `login_with_pin()`) — reusing it as an actual stored `hashed_password` would let anyone reading the source log in as that account, since the plaintext behind a fixed hash is knowable by definition. Every PIN-login-only `User` created by `generate_pin` instead gets `secrets.token_urlsafe(32)` hashed once and immediately discarded — never returned, never logged, structurally unusable as a real password since nobody chose it. This distinction was flagged proactively by a Plan sub-agent during this stage's planning and is documented inline at the call site in `AuthService`/`StudentService`, not just here.

`AuthService.login_with_pin()` replicates `login()`'s oracle-defense shape line for line: always calls `verify_password` against *some* hash (`student.pin_hash` if present, else `DUMMY_PASSWORD_HASH`) regardless of whether the student/PIN/link exists, and raises the identical `InvalidCredentialsError` for every failure branch (no such student, no PIN set, no linked user, wrong PIN, inactive account). `AuthService.__init__` gained a `StudentRepository` dependency — the first place `auth` depends on `students`, a new one-way fan-in edge consistent with every other cross-domain dependency in this codebase (never a cycle).

Credential issuance (`POST /students/{id}/credentials`, ADMIN-only) returns a new `StudentCredentialsRead{student_number, pin}` — the raw PIN appears in this one response only. If the student has no linked `User` yet, one is created and linked using the same flush-then-shared-commit atomicity pattern (`commit=False` on both writes, one final commit, rollback on failure) already established by `UserRepository`/`AuditLogRepository`, extended here to `StudentRepository`. If a `User` is already linked, the endpoint reuses it — the same route doubles as a PIN reset with no separate reset endpoint needed. PINs are generated via `secrets.randbelow(1_000_000)` (CSPRNG, not `random`), zero-padded to 6 digits, hashed via the existing `hash_password()`.

**Accepted residual risk, stated explicitly rather than silently ignored:** rate limiting in this codebase is per-IP only (slowapi, `get_remote_address`), not per-account, and `student_number` is a small, sequential, enumerable space. Combined with a 6-digit PIN, this is a materially weaker floor than the email+password path (email is not enumerable in the same structural way). Judged acceptable for this project's current scale and threat model, not a gap to silently paper over — a future per-account or per-student_number lockout would be the natural next hardening step if this codebase's threat model changes.

### Profile pictures (Student and Teacher)
Local Docker-volume storage + FastAPI `StaticFiles`, not S3/MinIO or bytea-in-Postgres — proportionate to this project's scale and consistent with its all-in-Docker-Compose shape (same reasoning as ADR 0003's containerized dev workflow). New `sms_uploads_data` named volume, same shape as the existing `sms_db_data` (persistent runtime data, not source — the existing narrow-bind-mount reasoning for `alembic/versions` is preserved, nothing new bind-mounted).

`src/sms/core/file_storage.py`'s `save_profile_picture()`: content-type allowlist (`image/jpeg`, `image/png`, `image/webp`, mapped to their file extensions — the mapping is load-bearing, not just an allowlist, since the extension is needed to build the stored filename), a 5MB size cap enforced via bounded-chunk reads (rejects mid-stream once the cap is exceeded, never buffers the whole file first), and a **deterministic filename derived from the entity's UUID**, never the client-supplied filename — avoids path traversal and gives a clean replace-on-reupload with no orphan bookkeeping. Deliberate deviation from the plan's literal wording: the upload directory is created lazily at write-time inside this function, not at module-import time, to avoid an import-time filesystem side effect; `main.py`'s own `mkdir` before the `StaticFiles` mount covers the startup-time requirement instead.

Both new upload routes (`POST /students/{id}/profile-picture`, `POST /teachers/{id}/profile-picture`) are ADMIN-only, matching each domain's existing mutation tier. Closed a real gap while touching `delete()` on both `StudentService` and `TeacherService`: best-effort-unlinks the stored file (`missing_ok=True`) when `profile_picture_path` is set, so deleting a Student/Teacher no longer orphans an image on disk forever.

### `GET /students/me`
Mirrors `GET /teachers/me` exactly, including the literal-path-before-`/{student_id}` registration-order requirement already documented there. New `StudentHasNoLinkedRecordError` mirrors `TeacherHasNoLinkedRecordError`. A student's own grades/assessments needed no new work — `GET /grades` already self-scopes for `STUDENT`-role callers (built in the Stage 7 assessments domain).

## Security review findings and fixes

`security-auditor` reviewed the implementation before this stage was called done (per this project's standing rule for auth/RBAC-touching changes) and found 4 confirmed issues, all applied directly (no real tradeoff — each closes an actual hole, none changed a tested-for behavior):

- **High — role confusion in PIN login.** `login_with_pin` never checked that the `User` linked to a `Student` actually had `role=STUDENT`. Separately, `StudentUpdate.user_id` (and `StudentCreate.user_id`) let any `ADMIN`/`TEACHER` re-link a student row's `user_id` to *any* existing user's id, with no role validation on the target. Chained together: a `TEACHER` could relink a student row to an `ADMIN`'s `user_id`, and a routine PIN issuance/reset on that student would then hand out valid login credentials for the admin account via `/auth/login-pin`. Fixed in two places — `AuthService.login_with_pin` now rejects a linked user whose role isn't `STUDENT`, and `StudentService` gained `_require_student_role_user()`, called from both `create()` and `update()` whenever `user_id` is set, raising `UserNotFoundError` (reusing the `users` domain's existing exception, matching the established cross-domain FK-validation pattern already used by `classes/service.py`) if the target doesn't exist or isn't a `STUDENT`.
- **Medium — content-type spoofing on profile-picture upload.** `file_storage.save_profile_picture` validated only the client-supplied `Content-Type` header, which is fully attacker-controlled — a spoofed header could get arbitrary bytes accepted and served back from `/uploads`. Fixed with magic-byte verification: the first chunk read is checked against real JPEG/PNG/WebP signatures and must match the declared type, or `InvalidFileTypeError` is raised before anything is written to disk. This is a genuine tradeoff the user was asked about explicitly (not applied silently) — it required rewriting `qa-engineer`'s test fixtures, which had used placeholder bytes like `b"fake-jpeg-bytes"` rather than real image signatures; the user chose to add the real fix over the cheaper alternatives (a bare `nosniff` header, or accepting the gap). Test fixtures across `tests/core/test_file_storage.py`, `tests/domains/students/{unit,integration}/`, and `tests/domains/teachers/integration/test_router.py` were updated to use minimal real magic-byte-prefixed payloads. Also closed a real coverage gap found in the same pass: the teacher profile-picture upload route had zero test coverage (happy path, wrong type, RBAC, 404) — added, mirroring the students file's existing pattern.
- **Medium — timing side-channel in PIN login.** `login_with_pin` performed a variable number of DB queries depending on whether `student_number` existed (one query when it didn't, two-plus when it did), unlike `login()` which always performs exactly one regardless of outcome — a measurable timing delta letting an attacker distinguish "no such student_number" from "exists" before ever touching the PIN, undercutting the oracle-defense the code's own comment claimed. Fixed by always performing the second lookup, using a fresh random UUID (`uuid4()`) in place of a real `user_id` when there's no linked user, so every branch performs the same `get_by_student_number` + `get(user_id)` pair.
- **Low — unhandled email collision in `generate_pin`.** Creating a linked `User` for a PIN-only account had no email-uniqueness pre-check, so a collision surfaced as a raw, untranslated `IntegrityError` (a 500) instead of a clean conflict. Fixed with the same pre-check pattern already used elsewhere in this file — `StudentAlreadyExistsError` on collision.

Two further findings were genuine tradeoffs, not silently decided — presented to the user, who chose:
- **Rate limiting on `/auth/login-pin` stays as originally planned** (5/minute per-IP, same as email login), even after the auditor reframed the residual risk more strongly (student_number's small/sequential/enumerable space + a distributed multi-IP attacker isn't meaningfully slowed by a per-IP-only limit, unlike email addresses which aren't structurally guessable). Documented here as a knowingly accepted limitation, not an oversight — a future per-`student_number` lockout would be the natural next step if this project's threat model changes.
- **Profile-picture content verification uses real magic-byte checking** (see above) rather than the cheaper `nosniff`-header-only option or leaving the gap — the user's explicit call given the two other options on the table.

## Consequences
- `auth` now depends on `students` in addition to `users` — a new one-way fan-in edge, not a cycle, consistent with every other cross-domain dependency in this codebase.
- The `secrets.token_urlsafe(32)` → hash → discard pattern for "structurally unusable password" is now precedent for any future PIN-only or non-password credential path — reuse it rather than reaching for `DUMMY_PASSWORD_HASH` outside its one intended use (failure-path timing equalization).
- The per-IP-only / enumerable-student_number residual risk on `/auth/login-pin` is accepted for now but should be revisited if this project's threat model changes (e.g. before any real production deployment) — a per-account lockout or CAPTCHA would be the natural next step.
- `file_storage.save_profile_picture()`'s entity-ID-based filename convention (`{subdir}/{entity_id}.{ext}`) is now the established pattern for any future upload feature in this codebase.
- A seed/demo-data script remains a confirmed, separate follow-up (not part of this stage) — revisits ADR 0020's earlier decline now that a real frontend exists to develop against.
- 489/489 tests passing (439 pre-Stage-9 + 45 new for student_number generation, PIN login's oracle-defense parity, PIN-generation's atomic two-write behavior, profile-picture content-type/size rejection, and file-deletion-on-entity-delete cleanup, + 5 added during the security-review pass: content-type-spoofing rejection and the previously-missing teacher profile-picture upload coverage), independently re-verified by rebuilding and re-running the full suite directly at each step, not inferred from any subagent's own report. One test-only fix applied before the security review: `test_allowed_content_types_matches_contract` asserted `ALLOWED_CONTENT_TYPES` was a plain set of strings; the production implementation is a dict (content-type → extension), which every other test in the same file already exercises correctly via the extension-derivation behavior — corrected the one assertion to match, no production code changed. A second test-only gap found by the role-check fix: a unit test had been linking a student to a `user_id` that was never backed by any real fake `User` at all (`user_id=uuid4()`) — the new validation correctly caught this as a real, previously-unenforced gap; fixed by creating a proper fake `STUDENT`-role user first.
- `security-auditor` reviewed the new authentication path and credential-issuance logic before this stage was called done — see "Security review findings and fixes" above for the full results and fixes applied.
